minimalsanitized.rationale: initWallet is public with NO initialization guard. Anyone can call this directly on the library contract (not via delegatecall) to become an owner. The function should have require(!initialized) but doesn't.

Executes selfdestruct which destroys the library contract. This is the destructive action enabled by the root cause (unprotected initWallet), not the root cause itself. The selfdestruct is correctly guarded by isOwner check - it's only exploitable because ownership can be hijacked via CA1.
Sets initialized flag but happens AFTER ownership is granted, and there's no require(!initialized) check at function entry. This allows repeated reinitialization.
Grants owner status. Prerequisite because this enables the attacker to pass the isOwner check in kill() after calling initWallet().
Checks if caller is owner, but this is insufficient because anyone can become owner by calling unprotected initWallet() first. Guard is present but bypassable.
Clears previous owner status. Part of reinitialization logic.
Clears owners array. Part of reinitialization logic.
Validates owner address is not zero. Correctly implemented.
Prevents duplicate owners. Correctly implemented.
Adds owner to array. Correctly implemented.
Event emission for logging.
Sets required signatures. Correctly implemented.
Event emission for logging before destruction.
Returns owner status. View function, correctly implemented.
Access control in execute(). Correctly implemented.
External call in execute(). Protected by owner check, correctly implemented.
Checks external call success. Correctly implemented.
Sets library address in proxy constructor. Correctly implemented.
Delegatecall to library. The proxy itself is correct; the issue is the library being destroyable.
